clue.text: I'll hate pic that's badly restored (referring to a certain collection)

indicators.note: a picture badly restored has its parts put back in the wrong order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, giving I, L, L

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a painting has been botched in restoration, with a bracketed aside about a collector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly restored' shuffles the ten letters of I'LL HATE PIC; the bracketed phrase, which looks like an aside, is the definition. 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Philately is stamp collecting, so the adjective describes something relating to that particular hobby collection.

clue.text: Write your name and position as an indicator

parts.note: to sign is to write your name
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: Advice to put your signature and job title on a form as an identifying mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A signpost is a marker pointing the way, so it serves as an indicator of direction.

clue.text: Proposal before meeting producing action

definitions.meaning: a formal proposal put before a meeting for debate

explanation.surface: An agenda item is tabled at a meeting and leads to something being done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' is a link joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion is a formal proposal at a meeting, and also movement or action in general.

clue.text: Standard sink?

definitions.meaning: a standard is a banner or ensign
to sink in the sense of droop or lose energy, as spirits do

explanation.definitionFit: A flag is a banner like a regimental standard, and to flag is to tire or sink in vigour.

clue.text: Take the stock in, but don't take it out!

definitions.text: Take the stock in, but don't take it out!

parts.words: Take the stock in, but don't take it out!
parts.note: taking the stock in means looking over a shop's goods, and not taking it out means buying nothing: browsing displays without purchase

explanation.definitionFit: To browse goods in shop windows only, looking at the stock without buying anything to carry away.

clue.text: The old one for pressing novice to cut the sweet

indicators.note: the novice's word cuts into the sweet, splitting it open

parts.note: a flan is a sweet tart or dessert
a tiro is a beginner

explanation.surface: A recipe step: let a beginner slice the dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' has the beginner's word split the dessert open; 'The old one for pressing' looks like an old person, but means an old-fashioned iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatiron was an old heavy iron, heated on a stove and used for pressing clothes.

clue.text: Sweeper adjusted boiler

indicators.note: an adjusted boiler has been altered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleaner tweaks the central-heating boiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' rearranges BOILER. A sweeper in football is the free defender behind the back line.
explanation.definitionFit: Libero is the Italian-derived football term for a sweeper, a defender playing behind the back line.

clue.text: A quiet year, but rather grey

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A calm year passed, though a somewhat dull one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash-coloured means pale grey, so ashy describes something rather grey in tone.

clue.text: Hoop I'll bend round — one for the masses

indicators.note: to bend the words is to twist them out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, giving I, L, L
a round shape resembles the letter O
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A child's toy hoop is bent into shape, one being made for everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bend' looks like a verb for shaping the hoop; it is the anagram signal, and 'round' and 'one' each add a letter after the rearranged part. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoi polloi is a Greek phrase used in English for ordinary people, the common masses.

clue.text: Student with affected manner retreats

parts.note: L is the learner plate, standing for a student driver
airs are pretentious, affected mannerisms, as in 'putting on airs'

explanation.surface: A pretentious student withdraws.
explanation.definitionFit: Lairs are animals' dens, places of retreat, so the plural noun matches retreats.

clue.text: Coming down a level between flights

definitions.meaning: an aircraft's touchdown or descent to the ground
the floor area between two flights of stairs

explanation.definitionFit: A landing is both an aircraft coming down to earth and the platform between flights of stairs.

clue.text: Indecisive article right to go into non-professional work?

indicators.note: the article and the right are placed inside the other piece

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is amateur home improvement
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone can't decide whether a newspaper piece belongs in an amateur project.
explanation.walkthrough: THE and R go into DIY, between DI and Y. DIY is British shorthand for do-it-yourself home repairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Dithery describes someone who dithers, wavering and unable to make up their mind.

clue.text: Course of river in Scottish town

indicators.note: the river's letter is placed within the Scottish word

parts.note: toon is the Scots form of town

explanation.surface: The path of a river through a town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like the river's route; it is a golf course. Royal Troon is a championship golf course on Scotland's Ayrshire coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Troon is a famous Scottish golf course, host of the Open Championship, so it is an example of a course.

clue.text: AB has towrope prepared for the vessel

indicators.note: towrope and AB are made ready in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; AB is also an able seaman

explanation.surface: An able seaman has a towing line ready for a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges AB plus TOWROPE. 'has' and 'for the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerboat is a fast motorboat, a type of vessel driven by a powerful engine.

clue.text: College haunts put out of order: a bloomer?

parts.note: a poly is a polytechnic, a type of college

indicators.note: the word haunts is put out of its order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student's favourite hangouts get disrupted, and someone wonders if it's a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bloomer' looks like a mistake; it is a flowering plant. POLY, short for polytechnic, was a type of British higher-education college.
explanation.definitionFit: The polyanthus is a garden primula grown for its flowers, so it is literally a bloomer.

clue.text: Post the rig possibly used by acrobats

indicators.note: possibly signals that the words could be arranged another way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Circus equipment: the pole and the rigging set up for performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tightropes are taut high wires on which circus acrobats walk and balance.

clue.text: Way of looking at problem from the side?

definitions.text: Way of looking at problem from the side?

parts.words: Way of looking at problem from the side?
parts.note: an approach to a puzzle that comes at it sideways, with 'from the side' read literally as a sideways glance

explanation.definitionFit: This is a creative, indirect approach to problem solving, coming at the issue from an unexpected angle.

clue.text: Research concerning insect is strong

parts.note: res is the abbreviation for research
on means about or concerning
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A study of a certain bug proves powerful.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonant voice or sound is deep and strong, ringing out clearly.

clue.text: One of enduring fame, but wrong about time

indicators.note: the word for wrong goes about, or around, the time letter

parts.note: immoral means morally wrong

explanation.surface: A celebrated figure who was nevertheless mistaken about the date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tells you the time letter goes inside the word for wrong. 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An immortal is someone whose fame lasts forever, a legendary figure remembered through the ages.

clue.text: Crook's instrument used to follow game

indicators.note: the instrument comes after the game in the answer

parts.note: cards is a game
a harp is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A villain's musical instrument accompanies a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a swindler who cheats at cards, so a type of crook.

clue.text: State in order regarding situation, they say

parts.note: re means regarding or about

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is heard, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: a site is a situation or location

explanation.surface: A formal request to declare things in sequence about a location, as people put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' signals a homophone: the word for situation is replaced by one that sounds the same but means to quote.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to list or recount items in order, stating them one after another.

clue.text: Accept grant

definitions.meaning: to concede that something is true

explanation.definitionFit: To admit is both to let someone in, accepting them, and to concede or grant a point.

clue.text: A politician comes over before the current measure

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A politician turns up before the electricity reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes over' is a link. 'current' looks like 'present'; it is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere is the unit in which electric current is measured.

clue.text: Head pursuing two companies — a fair prize?

indicators.note: the head comes after the two companies, chasing them

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, taken twice
CO is the abbreviation for company, taken twice
nut is slang for head

explanation.surface: A leader chasing two businesses, wondering if it's a fair reward.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a fairground stall where a coconut is the prize for knocking one off its stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Coconuts are the traditional prize at a fairground coconut shy, so it is a fair prize.

clue.text: Some scuba divers seen in the Caribbean

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used, a run within it

explanation.surface: A few divers are spotted in Caribbean waters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean Sea, so it is found there.

clue.text: Seaport works used to make paper etc

indicators.note: works means the word is worked over, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A harbour factory turns out paper products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like a noun, factories; it rearranges SEAPORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough grass whose fibres are used to make paper, rope and baskets.

clue.text: Finishes in tears, but not at first

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for tears is dropped

parts.note: rends means tears apart

explanation.surface: Something concludes in weeping, though not right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' looks like crying; it means rips, RENDS. 'in' and 'but' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends as a verb means finishes or concludes.

clue.text: Rod's to continue the innings

definitions.meaning: read as 'rod is': a short stick such as a conductor's or relay runner's
in cricket, to carry on batting rather than declare or be out

explanation.surface: A man named Rod is going to keep batting at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a man's name; it is a stick. Read as two words, the answer means to keep batting; in cricket an innings is a side's turn to bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short stick or rod, such as a conductor's or relay runner's.

clue.text: Don't give full credit below a certain price

parts.note: under means below
a rate is a fixed price or charge

explanation.surface: Advice not to award complete credit for anything under a set cost.
explanation.definitionFit: To underrate is to undervalue, not giving something the full credit it deserves.
